scenario_en: A broker cluster wants a partition to keep serving reads and writes after its leader dies; replicas are placed on different brokers.
q: 哪种复制策略最贴近？
q_en: Which replication strategy fits best?
options: leader-follower 多副本，失败时选新 leader
所有消息只写 leader 内存，不同步到其他 broker
每个消费者复制一份 broker 二进制文件来假装有副本
只在 metadata DB 里记录消息长度，不保存消息内容
options_en: Leader-follower replication with multiple replicas and leader election on failure.
Write every message only to leader memory with no broker replica.
Every consumer copies the broker binary and treats that as replication.
Record only message length in the metadata database, not the message.
why: leader-follower 让一个 leader 处理该 partition 的顺序写入，follower 保持可接管副本。常见会跨 broker 放 3 份左右副本，用存储成本换故障恢复。
why_en: Leader-follower replication gives each partition an ordered leader and recoverable followers.
whenOtherWins: 如果消息可丢且追求极低成本，副本数可以降低，但耐久性会下降。
tradeoff: 故障恢复能力 vs 副本存储和复制流量
optionExplanations: 每个分区由一个节点处理有序写入，另外几个节点保持同步副本，一旦这个节点挂了就能从副本里选出新的接手者。
只写 leader 内存不同步给其他 broker，leader 一宕机，未同步的数据就直接丢了。
消费者复制 broker 二进制文件跟数据副本毫无关系，这不构成真正的复制。
元数据库只记消息长度、不存内容，等于没有保存消息本体，谈不上可恢复。
optionExplanations_en: One node handles ordered writes for each partition while a few others keep synced copies, so a new one can take over from the copies once that node dies.
Writing only to leader memory with no sync to other brokers means anything unsynced is lost the moment the leader dies.
A consumer copying the broker binary has nothing to do with replicating data — that isn't real replication.
Recording only message length in the metadata DB, not the content, means nothing is actually recoverable.

q: pub-sub broker 集群里的 cluster manager 通常负责什么？
q_en: What does a pub-sub broker cluster manager usually handle?
options: 维护 broker 到 topic/partition 的注册信息
监控 broker 健康并在 leader 失败时触发选主
管理副本放置和跨 broker 复制关系
替消费者执行业务回调代码
options_en: Maintain broker-to-topic or partition registry information.
Monitor broker health and trigger leader election on failure.
Manage replica placement and replication relationships across brokers.
Run consumer business callback code for them.
why: cluster manager 是 broker 集群控制面，负责知道谁承载什么以及失败后怎么接管。消费者业务逻辑仍在消费者服务里。
why_en: The cluster manager is the broker control plane, not the place where consumer business logic runs.
optionExplanations: 知道每个 broker 承载哪些 topic/partition，是集群控制面最基础的登记信息。
监控 broker 健康状态，一旦 leader 失败就触发选主，是控制面的故障响应职责。
决定副本放在哪些 broker 上、怎么跨机复制，也是集群管理器要管的编排工作。
消费者的业务回调代码始终跑在消费者服务里，集群管理器不该替它执行业务逻辑。
optionExplanations_en: Knowing which broker owns which topic/partition is the most basic registry a cluster control plane keeps.
Monitoring broker health and triggering leader election on failure is the control plane's failure-response job.
Deciding where replicas live and how they replicate across brokers is also cluster-manager orchestration work.
Consumer business callback code always runs in the consumer service — the cluster manager shouldn't execute it instead.
scenario: broker 集群有 200 台机器、上千 partition；某个 leader 宕机后要在秒级恢复读写。
scenario_en: The broker cluster runs 200 machines and thousands of partitions, and when a leader dies reads and writes must come back within seconds.
diagram:
flowchart TB
  CM["Cluster manager 控制面"] --> R["broker/topic 注册信息"]
  CM --> H["健康监控与选主"]
  CM --> P["副本放置与复制关系"]
  BR["Broker 数据面"] --> L["topic log 读写"]
  CS["Consumer 服务"] --> BIZ["业务回调代码"]

q: consumer manager 在 broker 型 pub-sub 中负责哪些事？
q_en: What does the consumer manager handle in broker-based pub-sub?
options: 校验消费者是否有权限读某个 topic
阻止消费者读取已过 retention 的消息
保存或协调消费者的 offset 状态
替代 broker 存储所有 topic log
options_en: Verify whether a consumer may read a topic.
Prevent consumers from reading messages past retention.
Store or coordinate consumer offset state.
Replace brokers as the storage for all topic logs.
why: consumer manager 管的是读权限、保留期边界和消费进度，不是消息日志本体。这样 broker 可以专注 append 和读取，控制逻辑单独演进。
why_en: The consumer manager owns read authorization, retention boundaries, and offsets, while brokers store the logs.
optionExplanations: 先校验这个消费者是否有权限读这个 topic，是控制读取访问的第一步。
挡住消费者读取已经超过保留期的消息，避免读到本该被清理的数据。
保存或协调消费者的 offset 状态，让它知道自己读到哪、该从哪继续。
topic 日志的持久存储始终是 broker 的职责，这一层只管读权限、保留边界和消费进度，不该替代日志本体。
optionExplanations_en: Checking whether this consumer may read this topic is the first step in controlling read access.
Blocking reads past the retention window keeps consumers from reading data that should already be gone.
Storing or coordinating a consumer's offset state is what lets it know where it left off.
Durable topic-log storage is always the broker's job; this layer only owns read permission, retention boundaries, and progress — it shouldn't replace the log itself.
scenario: 多个消费者读同一 topic 且进度不同，超过 7 天保留期的消息不能再被读到。
scenario_en: Several consumers read the same topic at different progress points, and messages older than the seven-day retention window must no longer be readable.

scenario: 一个订阅者处理能力波动很大；系统既希望实时，又不能在消费者变慢时把它压垮。
scenario_en: A subscriber's processing capacity fluctuates; the system wants real-time delivery but must not overload a slow consumer.
q: push 和 pull 的取舍该怎么说？
q_en: How should you explain the push-versus-pull tradeoff?
options: push 延迟低但可能压垮慢消费者；pull 让消费者按能力取但可能多一点拉取延迟
push 和 pull 完全相同，都由 broker 和消费者同时控制节奏
pull 一定不能做实时系统，因为消费者永远不会主动读取
push 一定比 pull 更省资源，因为 broker 只发一次就不用再保留任何消息状态
options_en: Push has lower latency but can overload slow consumers; pull lets consumers pace reads but may add fetch latency.
Push and pull are exactly the same, with both sides controlling pace at once.
Pull can never support real-time systems because consumers never actively read.
Push always uses fewer resources than pull because the broker sends once and keeps no message state afterward.
why: push 把节奏掌握在系统侧，适合低延迟通知；pull 把节奏交给消费者，天然有背压。实际系统常让订阅者按场景选择。
why_en: Push favors immediacy, while pull gives consumers backpressure control.
whenOtherWins: 如果消费者都是稳定在线且需要极低延迟，push 可以更合适；如果消费者能力不可控，pull 更安全。
tradeoff: 实时推送 vs 消费者背压控制
optionExplanations: 由系统主动推送时延迟最低，但消费者慢了容易被压垮；换成消费者主动来取，节奏由它自己掌控，只是多一点轮询延迟。
push 由系统侧推、pull 由消费者侧拉，节奏控制方完全不同，说两者完全相同是错的。
pull 一样能支撑接近实时的系统，只是消费者要更频繁地主动拉取，不是永远做不到。
push 仍需重试和 ack 来应对慢消费者和失败，broker 也要保留状态；它并不天然更省资源。
optionExplanations_en: Having the system push gives the lowest latency but risks overwhelming a slow consumer; letting the consumer pull instead puts it in control of pace, at the cost of a little fetch latency.
Push is driven by the system side and pull by the consumer side — pacing control differs completely, so calling them identical is wrong.
Pull can still support near-real-time delivery if consumers fetch frequently enough — it's not permanently disqualified.
Push still needs retries and acks for slow consumers and failures, and the broker still keeps state; it is not inherently cheaper.

scenario: 消费者重启后要从上次处理的位置继续读；offset 更新很频繁，需要低延迟键值读写。
scenario_en: After restart, a consumer must resume from its last processed position; offsets update frequently and need low-latency key-value reads and writes.
q: offset 状态适合放在哪里？
q_en: Where should offset state be stored?
options: key-value store 保存消费 offset
只存在消费者进程栈里，重启后从随机位置继续
写进每条消息的 payload 并覆盖原始业务数据
存在负载均衡器健康检查里，和消费者无关
options_en: A key-value store for consumer offsets.
Only on the consumer process stack, then resume randomly after restart.
Inside each message payload, overwriting the original business data.
Inside load balancer health checks, unrelated to the consumer.
why: offset 是频繁更新的小状态，key-value store 能按 consumer/topic/partition 快速读写。只放内存会在重启后丢进度，导致跳读或大范围重放。
why_en: Offsets are small, frequently updated state that fit a key-value store and survive consumer restarts.
whenOtherWins: 如果消费者是一次性脚本且可从头重放，内存 offset 可以临时使用。
tradeoff: 可恢复消费进度 vs 状态存储成本
optionExplanations: 这类状态更新频繁但体积很小，用键值存储按各个消费者、topic 和分区分别存取，进程重启后也能接着上次的位置继续读。
只存在进程栈里，进程一重启栈就清空，消费者只能从随机位置继续，等于丢了进度。
写进消息 payload 会覆盖原始业务数据，offset 是消费侧状态，不该混进消息本体。
负载均衡器的健康检查跟消费者的读取进度完全是两个不相关的系统。
optionExplanations_en: This state updates often but stays small; a key-value store gives fast per-consumer/topic/partition reads and writes that survive a process restart.
Keeping it only on the process stack means a restart wipes it, so the consumer resumes from a random spot — effectively losing progress.
Writing it into the message payload overwrites the original business data; offset is consumer-side state and shouldn't be mixed into the message body.
Load balancer health checks and a consumer's read progress are two completely unrelated systems.

scenario: 团队给普通 topic 设置默认 7 天保留期，但允许 banking、审计等 topic 单独拉长。
scenario_en: The team sets a default 7-day retention for ordinary topics but lets banking or audit topics extend it.
q: 这个数字在设计里应该怎么使用？
q_en: How should this number be used in the design?
options: 把 7 天当默认策略，并让业务 topic 覆盖它
把 7 天当所有场景不可改的物理定律
把 7 天当作所有 topic 都必须精确保留的强制上限，不允许调短
因为有 7 天保留期就不需要删除任务
options_en: Treat 7 days as a default policy that business topics can override.
Treat 7 days as an unchangeable physical law for all cases.
Treat 7 days as a mandatory exact retention ceiling that no topic may shorten.
Skip deletion jobs because retention is 7 days.
why: 7 天是产品策略默认值，不是公式推导结果；它约束清理任务和可重放窗口。不同合规或成本要求的 topic 应覆盖默认值。
why_en: Seven days is a default policy that drives cleanup and replay windows, not a universal law.
whenOtherWins: 如果 topic 是短命指标或强合规账本，保留期应按业务改短或改长。
tradeoff: 默认可重放窗口 vs topic 级成本控制
optionExplanations: 7 天是产品定的默认策略，不是物理定律，银行、审计这类 topic 可以按合规或成本需求单独覆盖它。
把保留期当成不可改的物理定律，会让真正需要更长审计窗口的 topic 没法调整策略。
7 天是默认值不是强制上限，不同合规或成本的 topic 应能覆盖它，调长或调短都可以。
有保留期不代表不需要清理，过期数据依然要靠删除任务定期回收磁盘。
optionExplanations_en: Seven days is a product-chosen default, not a physical law — banking or audit topics can override it for compliance or cost reasons.
Treating retention as an unchangeable physical law leaves topics that genuinely need a longer audit window with no way to adjust.
Seven days is a default, not a mandatory ceiling; topics with different compliance or cost needs should be able to override it either way.
Having a retention period doesn't mean skipping cleanup — data past its window still needs a deletion job to reclaim disk.

scenario: 你要在面试里比较两种 pub-sub 设计：每个订阅者一个队列，或 broker 维护共享 topic log。
scenario_en: In an interview, you need to compare two pub-sub designs: one queue per subscriber or a broker-maintained shared topic log.
q: 百万订阅者、高吞吐小消息场景更偏向哪一个？
q_en: Which design better fits millions of subscribers and high-throughput small messages?
options: broker 共享 topic log
每个订阅者一个完整队列副本
同步调用所有订阅者
把消息存在每个客户端 cookie
options_en: A broker-backed shared topic log.
A full queue copy for every subscriber.
Synchronously call every subscriber.
Store messages in every client cookie.
why: 共享 topic log 避免把每条消息复制给每个订阅者，扩展性更好。代价是系统要实现 partition、offset、retention 和消费者管理。
why_en: A shared broker log avoids per-subscriber copies, which matters at very large fanout.
whenOtherWins: 如果订阅者很少、队列隔离是第一目标，per-subscriber queue 可以更快落地。
tradeoff: 低存储放大 vs 自研 broker 复杂度
optionExplanations: 所有订阅者共用同一份日志而不是各自复制，消息只需要落盘一次，这在百万订阅者规模下明显更省存储。
每个订阅者一份完整队列副本，订阅者一多，存储和元数据就跟着线性爆炸。
同步调用所有订阅者，只要有一个慢或挂了，整条发布路径就会被拖住。
把消息存进每个客户端 cookie，既没有可靠持久化，也扛不住百万订阅者规模。
optionExplanations_en: All subscribers share one log instead of each holding a copy, so a message is written once — a clear storage win at millions of subscribers.
A full queue copy per subscriber means storage and metadata explode linearly as subscribers grow.
Synchronously calling every subscriber means one slow or dead subscriber stalls the whole publish path.
Storing messages in every client cookie has no durable persistence and can't handle millions of subscribers.

scenario: 一个订单 topic 有 12 个 partition；订单处理服务启动 4 个实例，希望同一条消息只由组内一个实例处理，同时提高并行度。
scenario_en: An orders topic has 12 partitions; the order-processing service runs 4 instances and wants each message handled by one instance in the group while increasing parallelism.
q: 应使用什么消费模型？
q_en: Which consumption model should be used?
options: consumer group：组内分摊 partition
让 4 个实例都独立订阅并重复处理每条消息
让生产者同步调用 4 个实例并等待全部返回
把所有 partition 合成一个全局锁来降低并行度
options_en: A consumer group where instances split partition ownership.
Let all 4 instances subscribe independently and duplicate every message.
Make the producer synchronously call all 4 instances and wait for all.
Merge all partitions behind one global lock and reduce parallelism.
why: consumer group 的语义是组内一条 partition 通常只分给一个成员消费，从而避免组内重复处理。增加实例能提高并行度，但不会超过 partition 数量。
why_en: A consumer group shares partitions among instances so each message is handled once within the group.
whenOtherWins: 如果通知、搜索、分析都要各自收到同一事件，它们应是不同 consumer group 或不同订阅者。
tradeoff: 组内负载均衡 vs 跨组广播
diagram:
flowchart TB
  T["orders topic"] --> P0["p0"]
  T --> P1["p1"]
  T --> P2["p2"]
  T --> P3["p3"]
  subgraph G["consumer group: order-service"]
    C1["instance A"]
    C2["instance B"]
  end
  P0 --> C1
  P1 --> C1
  P2 --> C2
  P3 --> C2
optionExplanations: 同组内的实例分摊 12 个分区的所有权，4 个实例并行消费又不会有两个实例抢到同一条消息。
让每个实例都独立订阅，同一条消息会被 4 个实例各处理一遍，跟只处理一次的目标相反。
让生产者同步调用并等 4 个实例都返回，把异步消费硬生生变成了同步阻塞。
把所有分区合成一个全局锁，反而降低了并行度，跟提高并行度的目标正相反。
optionExplanations_en: Instances in the same group split ownership of the 12 partitions, so 4 of them consume in parallel without two ever grabbing the same message.
Letting every instance subscribe independently means all 4 process the same message, the opposite of handling it once.
Making the producer synchronously call and wait for all 4 instances turns async consumption into forced synchronous blocking.
Merging every partition behind one global lock actually reduces parallelism — the opposite of the goal.

scenario: consumer group 中一个实例宕机；它原来负责的 partition 还有未处理消息，其他实例仍在线。
scenario_en: One instance in a consumer group dies; it owned partitions with unprocessed messages, while other instances remain online.
q: 系统应发生什么恢复动作？
q_en: What recovery action should the system take?
options: 触发 rebalance，把孤儿分区分给存活实例，从已提交 offset 继续
删除这些 partition 里的全部消息，并假装已经处理成功
让生产者重新创建整个 topic，连同全部历史消息一起重建
永久停止该 consumer group，等待人工迁移全部 partition
options_en: Trigger a rebalance so live instances take the orphaned partitions from committed offsets.
Delete every message in those partitions and pretend the work already succeeded.
Have the producer recreate the entire topic along with all of its historical messages.
Stop the consumer group permanently and wait for a human to migrate every partition.
why: 正常路径是实例拥有 partition 并提交 offset；失败后 owner 消失，rebalance 重新分配，接管者从已提交位置继续。代价是提交点之后的消息可能重做，所以处理要幂等。
why_en: Rebalancing reassigns orphaned partitions and resumes from committed offsets, with possible duplicate processing.
whenOtherWins: 如果每个消费者都是独立广播订阅者，就不应把 partition 在组内互斥分配。
tradeoff: 自动故障接管 vs rebalance 抖动和重复处理

termDefinitions.meaning: rebalance 是 consumer group 成员变化后重新分配 partition 所有权。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A rebalance reassigns partition ownership after consumer group membership changes.

optionExplanations: 实例一宕机它名下的分区就没人管了，系统重新把这些分区分给还活着的实例，从上次确认过的位置继续读。
删掉这些分区的消息假装处理成功，等于把真实未处理的业务数据直接销毁。
让生产者重建整个 topic 和全部历史消息代价极高，而且这些历史本来就没有丢失。
永久停机等人工迁移，正常故障恢复本该自动完成，不需要停下来等人处理。
optionExplanations_en: Once an instance dies, its partitions have no owner, so the system hands them to live instances that resume from the last committed position.
Deleting those partitions and pretending success just destroys real, unprocessed business data.
Making the producer rebuild the whole topic and its history is extremely costly, and that history was never actually lost.
Stopping the group permanently for manual migration defeats the point — normal recovery should happen automatically, no waiting on a human.

scenario: 一个通知 topic 同时包含 email、SMS 和 push 事件；某些订阅者只想接收 type='email' 的消息。
scenario_en: A notifications topic contains email, SMS, and push events; some subscribers want only messages where type='email'.
q: 应如何支持过滤而不破坏 topic 抽象？
q_en: How can filtering be supported without breaking the topic abstraction?
options: metadata + subscription filter
让生产者为每个消费者单独调用一次并自己判断兴趣
要求订阅者读取所有消息并永久保存无关消息等待以后过滤
把过滤条件硬编码进 topic 名字，每种组合都新建一个独立 topic
options_en: Use metadata plus a subscription filter.
Have producers call every consumer separately and decide consumer interest themselves.
Force subscribers to read and permanently keep irrelevant messages for later filtering.
Hard-code filter conditions into topic names and create a separate topic for every combination.
why: 过滤条件属于订阅语义，放在 metadata 或订阅配置里能减少无关投递。代价是 broker 需要评估过滤规则，规则太复杂会影响吞吐。
why_en: Subscription filters reduce irrelevant delivery by matching message metadata before or during consumption.
whenOtherWins: 如果过滤规则很复杂且吞吐很高，让消费者本地过滤可能保护 broker 简单性。
tradeoff: 减少无关投递 vs broker 过滤成本

termDefinitions.meaning: metadata 是描述消息的附加字段，例如类型、时间、路由键或权限信息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Metadata is descriptive data attached to a message, such as type, time, routing key, or authorization data.

optionExplanations: 把过滤规则挂在消息的附加字段和订阅设置上，broker 投递前先按规则筛一遍，无关的消息就不会送到这个订阅者手里。
让生产者为每个消费者单独判断兴趣，等于把消费者的订阅偏好又耦合回了生产端。
要求订阅者读完再永久保存无关消息，broker 端反而更简单，但徒增了消费者的存储和处理负担。
为每种过滤组合建 topic 会导致 topic 数量爆炸且难维护；过滤应放在订阅的 metadata 里。
optionExplanations_en: Attach filter rules to the message's extra fields and the subscription config; the broker matches them before delivery so irrelevant messages never reach this subscriber.
Having the producer decide each consumer's interest individually recouples subscriber preferences back onto the producer.
Forcing subscribers to read and permanently keep irrelevant messages keeps the broker simple but dumps extra storage and processing onto consumers.
Creating a topic per filter combination explodes the topic count and is unmaintainable; filtering belongs in subscription metadata.

q: 消息重试到 DLQ 的完整状态链是什么？
q_en: What is the full state chain from retry to a dead-letter queue?
steps: 达到最大尝试次数后写入 DLQ
worker 领取消息并开始处理
处理失败，消息按策略延迟后重新可见或重新入队
运维或修复任务检查 DLQ 并决定重放、修数据或丢弃
重试计数增加并保留失败原因
why: 这条链要讲清楚失败不是直接消失：领取、失败、延迟重试、计数达上限、进 DLQ。代价是重复处理和积压监控，业务要幂等并告警。
why_en: Retries should preserve failure state, stop after a limit, and isolate poison messages in a dead-letter queue.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  M["Message"] --> W["Worker"]
  W -->|fail| Delay["Backoff delay"] --> Q["Retry queue"] --> W
  W -->|max attempts| D["DLQ"] --> Ops["Inspect / replay / discard"]

scenario: 支付扣款消费者可能重复收到同一扣款消息。产品不能接受重复扣款，也不想丢掉已接受的扣款请求。
scenario_en: A payment-charge consumer may receive the same charge message twice. The product cannot accept duplicate charges and also does not want to lose accepted requests.
q: 应怎样描述投递语义和业务保护？
q_en: How should delivery semantics and business protection be described?
options: 队列用至少一次投递，业务用幂等键保证同一 chargeId 只扣一次
只要队列叫 exactly-once，业务就不需要唯一键
改成最多一次投递，所有失败都静默丢弃
把 chargeId 幂等键放在队列层去重，就能同时保证投递和不重复扣款
options_en: Use at-least-once delivery and an idempotency key so one chargeId is charged once.
If the queue says exactly-once, the business needs no unique key.
Switch to at-most-once delivery and silently drop all failures.
Put the chargeId idempotency at the queue-layer dedup so it guarantees both delivery and no double charge.
why: 队列层很难单独承诺端到端 exactly-once，尤其跨数据库和外部支付网关。面试里更稳的是至少一次加业务幂等键，用 chargeId 挡重复副作用。
why_en: For payments, combine at-least-once delivery with a business idempotency key rather than trusting the queue alone.
whenOtherWins: 如果消息是可丢的指标采样，最多一次可以用更低成本换简单性。
tradeoff: 可靠投递 vs 重复副作用控制

termDefinitions.meaning: exactly-once 是端到端只生效一次的目标，通常需要队列、存储和业务操作共同配合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Exactly-once is the goal that an effect happens once end to end, usually requiring cooperation across queue, storage, and business logic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最多一次投递避免重复，但失败时可能丢消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: At-most-once delivery avoids duplicates but may lose messages on failure.

termDefinitions.meaning: chargeId 是一次扣款业务操作的唯一标识，可用于幂等扣款。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A chargeId is the unique identifier for one charge operation and can enforce idempotency.

optionExplanations: 端到端只生效一次很难只靠队列保证，更稳的做法是接受可能重复投递，再用 chargeId 这类幂等键在业务层挡住重复扣款。
队列标榜 exactly-once 不代表业务就不需要唯一键，跨数据库和外部网关的失败恢复仍可能产生重复调用。
改成最多一次投递、失败静默丢弃，会让本该成功的扣款请求直接消失，风险比重复更大。
队列层去重窗口有限且跨支付网关不可靠，幂等键必须落在扣款业务侧才能挡住重复副作用。
optionExplanations_en: A queue alone rarely guarantees a one-time effect end to end; the sturdier move is to accept possible redelivery and let a chargeId-style key block the duplicate charge in business logic.
A queue claiming exactly-once doesn't remove the need for a unique key — failure recovery across databases and an external gateway can still duplicate calls.
Switching to at-most-once and silently dropping failures makes a request that should have succeeded just vanish, riskier than a duplicate.
The queue's dedup window is limited and unreliable across the payment gateway; the idempotency key must live in the charging business logic to block duplicate side effects.

scenario: 一个热门队列的写入量突然暴涨，导致同 broker 上其他低流量队列的延迟也升高。
scenario_en: A hot queue's write rate spikes, and low-traffic queues on the same broker also see higher latency.
q: 应优先考虑哪种隔离手段？
q_en: Which isolation mechanism should be considered first?
options: 把热点队列迁到独立 broker 资源
把所有队列合并到一个更大的锁里并共享瓶颈
关闭低流量队列的监控来隐藏邻居影响
让消费者忽略延迟并继续堆积未处理消息
options_en: Move the hot queue onto dedicated broker resources.
Merge all queues behind one larger lock and share the bottleneck.
Disable monitoring for low-traffic queues to hide neighbor impact.
Ask consumers to ignore latency while backlog keeps growing.
why: 热点队列会抢磁盘、CPU 和网络资源，影响同机邻居。把它拆分或独立放置，可以用资源隔离保护其他队列的尾延迟。
why_en: Hot queues should be split or isolated so one workload does not steal broker resources from others.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是消费者太少导致积压，先加消费者可能比迁移 broker 更快。
tradeoff: 性能隔离 vs 迁移和运维成本

termDefinitions.meaning: tail latency 是高百分位请求延迟，例如 p95 或 p99。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Tail latency is high-percentile latency such as p95 or p99.

optionExplanations: 写入暴涨的队列会挤占同机磁盘、CPU 和网络带宽，把它挪到独立资源上，才能不让邻居队列的延迟跟着一起变差。
把所有队列合并进一个更大的锁，反而让热点队列的压力扩散给更多队列，隔离目标正相反。
关闭低流量队列的监控只是看不见问题，邻居队列的延迟并没有真的被解决。
让消费者忽略延迟、继续堆积未处理消息，只会让积压和延迟越来越严重。
optionExplanations_en: A queue whose writes spike ends up hogging the shared disk, CPU, and network; moving it to dedicated resources stops its neighbors' latency from degrading too.
Merging every queue behind one bigger lock spreads the hot queue's pressure onto more queues — the opposite of isolation.
Disabling monitoring for low-traffic queues just hides the symptom; the neighbor's latency problem is still there.
Telling consumers to ignore latency while backlog keeps growing only makes the buildup and delay worse.

scenario: broker 存储的是大量小消息；主要操作是追加新消息和按 offset 顺序读取。
scenario_en: The broker stores many small messages; the main operations are appending new records and reading sequentially by offset.
q: 磁盘布局应偏向哪种形式？
q_en: What disk layout should the broker prefer?
options: append-only 日志分段
每条消息随机覆盖同一行
每个消费者一个 Excel 文件
只存在进程堆内存
options_en: Append-only log segments.
Randomly overwrite the same row for every message.
One Excel file per consumer.
Only process heap memory.
why: 追加日志匹配 broker 的主要路径：顺序写入、按 offset 顺序读、按 segment 做保留期清理。它不适合随机更新单条历史消息，这正是消息不可变的代价。
why_en: Append-only segments match sequential writes, offset reads, and retention cleanup.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务要频繁更新单条记录字段，普通数据库表可能更合适。
tradeoff: 顺序 I/O 吞吐 vs 随机更新能力
codeSample:
topic=orders partition=3
segment-000001.log: offsets 0..999999
segment-000002.log: offsets 1000000..1999999
# retention can delete whole old segments
optionExplanations: broker 的主要操作是顺序追加新消息、按 offset 顺序读，append-only segment 正好匹配这个模式，还能整段删除做保留期清理。
随机覆盖同一行意味着旧消息直接被抹掉，跟保留历史消息供多消费者按 offset 读取的需求冲突。
给每个消费者建一个 Excel 文件既没有顺序写入性能，也没法支撑高吞吐小消息。
只存进程堆内存，进程一重启所有消息就没了，谈不上持久化。
optionExplanations_en: The broker's main operations are sequential appends and offset-ordered reads — append-only segments match that pattern and let retention delete whole old segments at once.
Randomly overwriting the same row erases old messages, conflicting with the need to keep history for consumers reading at different offsets.
One Excel file per consumer has neither sequential-write performance nor the ability to handle high-throughput small messages.
Storing only in process heap memory means a restart erases every message — there's no durability at all.

scenario: 队列系统上线后，用户抱怨通知延迟。你需要判断是生产变慢、broker 积压，还是消费者追不上。
scenario_en: After the queue system launches, users complain about notification delay. You need to tell whether producers are slow, brokers are backlogged, or consumers are behind.
q: 最应该监控哪组指标？
q_en: Which metrics should you monitor first?
options: 吞吐、depth、lag、retry/DLQ
只监控官网首页颜色和按钮圆角来推断消息延迟
只看消费者机器名长度和实例编号是否好记
只记录每条消息的字体和 UI 展示顺序
options_en: Throughput, depth, lag, retries, and DLQ counts.
Only monitor the marketing homepage color and button radius to infer queue delay.
Only inspect consumer machine-name length and whether instance numbers are memorable.
Only record each message's font and UI display order.
why: 这些指标能把延迟拆成写入速度、队列积压、消费能力和失败重试。没有 lag 和 DLQ，系统只知道慢了，却不知道压力卡在哪一段。
why_en: These metrics separate producer speed, backlog, consumer progress, and failure loops.
whenOtherWins: 如果问题是单个业务结果错误，还需要 trace 和业务日志定位消息内容。
tradeoff: 可观测性成本 vs 故障定位速度

termDefinitions.meaning: queue depth 是队列里尚未处理的消息数量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Queue depth is the number of messages waiting to be processed.

optionExplanations: 吞吐、队列积压、lag 和重试/DLQ 能把延迟拆成写入速度、积压位置和消费能力，才知道压力卡在哪一段。
首页颜色和按钮圆角是前端视觉细节，跟消息队列的延迟诊断毫无关系。
机器名长度好不好记跟消费者实际处理能力没有任何关联。
消息的字体和 UI 展示顺序不反映消息路径上的任何真实状态。
optionExplanations_en: Throughput, queue depth, lag, and retry/DLQ counts split latency into producer speed, backlog position, and consumer capacity, showing where the pressure actually sits.
Homepage color and button radius are frontend visual details with nothing to do with diagnosing queue delay.
How memorable a machine name is has no bearing on a consumer's actual processing capacity.
A message's font and UI display order reflect nothing about the real state of the message path.

q: 面试中设计 pub-sub 系统时，回答顺序怎样更完整？
q_en: In a pub-sub design interview, what answer order is more complete?
steps: 深入 broker、partition、replication、offset、retention 和失败恢复
先澄清 topic、publisher、subscriber、消息大小、保留期和投递语义
画高层路径：publish 到 topic，broker 存储，subscriber 或 group 读取
最后评估扩展性、可用性、耐久性、顺序和成本取舍
定义核心 API：create、write、subscribe、read、delete
why: 面试回答先定需求和 API，再画主路径，最后下钻关键取舍。这样不会一上来陷进 Kafka 细节，也不会漏掉保留期、顺序和投递语义。
why_en: Start with requirements and APIs, then draw the main path before diving into broker tradeoffs and evaluation.

scenario: 面试官让你总结分布式队列和 pub-sub 的共同评价维度，而不是再列组件名。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks you to summarize the shared evaluation dimensions for distributed queues and pub-sub, not just list components again.
q: 最好的总结角度是什么？
q_en: What is the best evaluation lens?
options: 按系统保证逐项讲取舍
只说用了很多服务器所以一定好，不解释任何保证或代价
只背诵所有 API 名字，不说明它们如何满足需求
只比较哪个产品名更流行，不讨论顺序或投递语义
options_en: Explain tradeoffs by system guarantees.
Say it must be good because it uses many servers, without explaining guarantees or costs.
Only recite all API names without explaining how they satisfy requirements.
Only compare which product name is more popular, ignoring ordering and delivery semantics.
why: 评价题要回到需求是否被满足，以及每个保证花了什么代价。顺序、投递语义、复制和分区是最容易互相牵制的几条轴。
why_en: Evaluate the design by guarantees and tradeoffs, especially where ordering, delivery, replication, and partitioning constrain each other.
whenOtherWins: 如果题目明确要求选型落地，再把这些维度映射到 Kafka、RabbitMQ、SQS 等具体产品。
tradeoff: 系统保证完整性 vs 组件清单式回答
optionExplanations: 评价要回到需求是否被满足、每个保证花了什么代价，顺序、投递语义、复制和分区这几条轴最容易互相牵制。
光说用了很多服务器就一定好，没有解释任何保证或代价，等于什么都没评价。
只背 API 名字不说明它们如何满足需求，面试官问的是取舍不是接口清单。
只比哪个产品名更流行，完全绕开了顺序和投递语义这些真正的技术判断。
optionExplanations_en: Evaluation should come back to whether requirements are met and what each guarantee costs — ordering, delivery semantics, replication, and partitioning constrain each other the most.
Saying it must be good because it uses many servers, without explaining any guarantee or cost, isn't really an evaluation at all.
Reciting API names without explaining how they satisfy requirements misses the point — the question is about tradeoffs, not an interface list.
Comparing which product name is more popular sidesteps the real technical judgment calls around ordering and delivery semantics.
